citation: NSPS, Surveying Profession Demographics Survey (n=2409). National Society of Professional Surveyors.
key_finding: 92.3% White; 94.3% male; only 8 Black respondents out of 2409; 42 Hispanic/Latino; 14 Native American; 16 Asian/Pacific Islander. Overwhelmingly homogeneous profession.
gap_limitation: No year published on document; convenience sample of NSPS members only (likely skews older/more credentialed); no comparison to labor force benchmarks; not peer-reviewed.

citation: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Current Population Survey Table 11: Employed persons by detailed occupation sex race and Hispanic or Latino ethnicity. BLS.
key_finding: Surveyors/cartographers/photogrammetrists workforce (2023): 82.8% male / 17.2% female; 83.1% White; 3.55% Black; 11.1% Hispanic. Total workforce ~35072.
gap_limitation: CPS sample sizes for small occupations can be volatile year-to-year; combines surveyors with cartographers and photogrammetrists into one category; no longitudinal trend analysis published by BLS for this specific occupation.

citation: Zippia, Registered Land Surveyor Demographics and Statistics [2025]. Zippia.com.
key_finding: Only 2.6% of registered land surveyors are female; 78.6% White; 9.2% Hispanic/Latino. Average age 43.
gap_limitation: Zippia aggregates from multiple sources without clear methodology; conflates different surveyor subcategories; not peer-reviewed.

citation: Zippia, Surveyor Demographics and Statistics [2025]. Zippia.com.
key_finding: 27.6% of surveyors (broadly defined) are women; 76.0% White; 10.6% Hispanic; 4.9% Asian. Women earn 96 cents per dollar earned by men in surveying.
gap_limitation: Broader definition of surveyor than licensed PLS; methodology not transparent; not peer-reviewed.

citation: CareerExplorer, Surveyor Demographics in the United States. CareerExplorer.com.
key_finding: Over 31979 surveyors employed in US; average age 43; more women interested in becoming surveyors than actually working as one suggesting barriers between interest and entry.
gap_limitation: Web aggregator; no original analysis; methodology unclear.

citation: Neville MRICS, Women in Surveying: A Review of the Statistics of Chartered Women Professionals and the Steps Being Taken to Address Diversity. LinkedIn article.
key_finding: RICS: 16% female Chartered Surveyors in Aug 2020 (up from 12% in 2012); 31% of new entrants are women; average female membership 16 years vs 28 years for men — women leave at age 47 vs men at 61.
gap_limitation: UK-focused (RICS); not peer-reviewed; does not address race/ethnicity; limited to chartered surveyors.

citation: PDH Academy, Women in Land Surveying: Where We've Been and Where We're Going. PDH Academy blog.
key_finding: Women now ~13% of land surveyor careers (up from 3% in the 1980s); 27% of surveying students are women; Alice Fletcher was first known American female surveyor in mid-1800s.
gap_limitation: Blog post; no original data analysis; does not address racial diversity.

citation: Funk C and Parker K, STEM Jobs See Uneven Progress in Increasing Gender Racial and Ethnic Diversity. Pew Research Center.
data_used: ACS PUMS microdata (IPUMS) 2014-2016 and 2017-2019 aggregated; NCES IPEDS
key_finding: Black workers 9% of STEM (vs 11% total workforce); Hispanic 15% of STEM (vs 18% total); women 15% of engineering/architecture cluster; no change in Black STEM share since 2016. Analysis at occupation-cluster level not individual occupation level.
gap_limitation: Does NOT break out surveyors specifically — groups them under broad engineering/architecture cluster. Methodology uses IPUMS ACS microdata but at aggregated occupation-cluster level only.

citation: Landivar LC, Disparities in STEM Employment by Sex Race and Hispanic Origin. American Community Survey Reports ACS-24. U.S. Census Bureau.
key_finding: Documented STEM employment disparities by sex race and Hispanic origin using ACS data; established baseline for demographic tracking of STEM workforce.
gap_limitation: Surveyor occupation likely included within broader category; over a decade old; does not provide occupation-level granularity for small occupations like surveying.

citation: Martinez A and Christnacht C, The Intersectionality of Sex Race and Hispanic Origin in the STEM Workforce. Working Paper SEHSD-WP2018-27. U.S. Census Bureau.
key_finding: Examined intersectionality of sex/race/Hispanic origin in STEM; noted that prior research rarely examines joint effects of these demographics in STEM occupations.
gap_limitation: Working paper (not peer-reviewed journal); does not single out surveying; broad STEM focus.

citation: World Geospatial Industry Council (WGIC), Diverse Workforce and Safe Work Environment Supercharge Geospatial Industry. WGIC.
key_finding: GIS workforce ~42% female overall; but only 28% female in startups and 32% in private sector; state government (41%) and nonprofit (45%) better balanced.
gap_limitation: Focuses on GIS/geospatial not land surveying specifically; does not address race/ethnicity in depth; industry self-report.

citation: GoGeomatics, Who Will Build the Future? Geomatics Workforce Missing from Canada's Infrastructure Ambitions. GoGeomatics.ca.
data_used: Canadian workforce data and program closure tracking
key_finding: Program closures + retiring workforce + outdated policies converging into workforce crisis; domestic awareness of geomatics almost nonexistent among students and guidance counsellors.
gap_limitation: Canada-focused; trade publication; no peer-reviewed methodology.

citation: GIM International, Why and How Does Geomatics Engineering Education Need to Change? GIM International.
key_finding: Enhancement of geomatics programs with new courses can increase diversity and inclusivity by broadening career pathways and attracting students from equity-deserving groups.
gap_limitation: Opinion/commentary piece; no quantitative diversity data.

citation: UN-GGIM, Inclusion and Diversity in Geospatial Information Management. Side event presentation 13th Session.
key_finding: Advocates for more diverse global geospatial workforce in terms of gender/race/religion/ability/neurodivergency; calls for national-level strategies.
gap_limitation: International focus; aspirational rather than empirical; no US surveyor-specific data.

citation: USGS, Diversity Equity Inclusion and Accessibility. USGS Office of Diversity and Equal Opportunity.
key_finding: USGS has formal DEIA office and programming for its geospatial/survey workforce.
gap_limitation: Government institutional page; no published research or data on surveyor demographics specifically.

citation: RPLS.com forum, Diversity in Land Surveying. RPLS.com forum discussion.
key_finding: Multiple practitioners note surveying is among least diverse professions; recruitment through personal networks (father/uncle/friend) reinforces homogeneity; some states report zero non-white surveyors.
gap_limitation: Forum discussion; anecdotal only; no systematic data; but reveals practitioner-level awareness of the problem.

citation: Allen & Company, How is the Surveying and Mapping Profession Evolving and Why? Allen-Company.com.
key_finding: Technology evolution opening doors to minorities and women who see opportunity in tech-driven surveying roles; not all work is fieldwork anymore.
gap_limitation: Industry blog; no data to support claims about diversity improvement; aspirational.

citation: Data USA, Surveyors Cartographers and Photogrammetrists. DataUSA.io.
key_finding: Interactive demographic profiles: 83.1% White; 82.8% male; median age and wage data; geographic distribution of workforce.
gap_limitation: Visualization tool not original research; combines surveyor subcategories; useful as data source not as citation.

citation: U.S. Census Bureau, Equal Employment Opportunity Tabulation 2014-2018 (5-year ACS data). Census.gov.
key_finding: Pre-tabulated race/sex by detailed occupation (236-237 categories) including surveyors/cartographers; available at national/state/CBSA/county level. Primary external benchmark for workforce composition analysis.
gap_limitation: Data exists but NO published analysis applying it specifically to surveyors has been found in the literature. Raw data available but requires custom extraction.

citation: NSF NCSES, The STEM Labor Force of Today: Scientists Engineers and Skilled Technical Workers. Science and Engineering Indicators. NSB-2021-2.
data_used: ACS; NSCG; IPEDS; multiple federal surveys
key_finding: Hispanic and Black workers underrepresented in S&E occupations at about half their workforce share; Asian workers overrepresented at 3x. Number of Hispanic S&E workers sextupled 1995-2019.
gap_limitation: Broad STEM/S&E focus; does not disaggregate to surveyor level; surveying may fall outside S&E definition used by NSF.

citation: NSF NCSES, The STEM Labor Force: Scientists Engineers and Skilled Technical Workers. Science and Engineering Indicators. NSB-2024-5.
key_finding: Updated STEM workforce diversity data through 2023; continued underrepresentation of Black and Hispanic workers in STEM.
gap_limitation: Same limitation as above — no surveyor-specific breakout.

citation: Pearson YE and Simmons DR, Diversity and Inclusion in Civil and Environmental Engineering. Journal of Professional Issues in Engineering Education and Practice 144(4).
journal_source: ASCE Journal of Professional Issues in Eng. Ed. and Practice
key_finding: Civil engineering bachelor's recipients overwhelmingly male and 60.1% White; Canon 8 added to ASCE Code of Ethics in 2017 to address inequities.
gap_limitation: Focuses on civil engineering not surveying; provides useful comparison point; no ACS microdata analysis.

citation: Shrestha BK et al., Diversity and Inclusion in the Engineering-Construction Industry. Journal of Management in Engineering 38(2). ASCE.
journal_source: ASCE Journal of Management in Engineering
data_used: BLS + Census Bureau + Data USA data
key_finding: Analyzed employment levels and wage distributions by gender in construction/engineering; construction industry facing significant labor shortage; increasing D&I imperative for future workforce.
gap_limitation: Civil engineering/construction focus not surveying; uses Census data but at industry not occupation level for surveying.

citation: STRUCTURE Magazine, Diversity in the Structural Engineering Profession.
data_used: ASCE membership data and firm surveys
key_finding: ~17% of structural engineers are women; 9% of SEI membership is women (lowest among ASCE institutes); fewer minorities than civil engineering overall.
gap_limitation: Structural engineering not surveying; useful comparison showing surveying likely even less diverse.

citation: Survey Review (Taylor & Francis), Trends and Challenges in Regulation and Accreditation of Land Surveying Professions in the United States of America and the United Kingdom.
data_used: Review of legal regulations and professional guidelines US/UK
key_finding: Shortage of professionals affects those already in profession; ongoing debate on regulation level; challenges in education including recruitment/retention of educators and addressing gender imbalance and diversity.
gap_limitation: Peer-reviewed but focused on regulation/accreditation not demographics per se; notes gender/diversity as a challenge without quantitative demographic analysis.

citation: Anonymous, Surveying Shortage: A Brief Look at the Evidence. Academia.edu.
key_finding: Shortage primarily an effect of general demographic decline in developed countries; exacerbated by 2008 recession + lack of awareness + lack of educational institutions + low pay + aging workforce + technology.
gap_limitation: Not peer-reviewed; working paper; no original demographic data collection; mentions diversity only tangentially.

citation: NGAC, Geospatial Workforce Development White Paper. Federal Geographic Data Committee.
key_finding: Geospatial technology identified as one of 14 sectors projected to add substantial new jobs; serious workforce development challenge with shortage of qualified workers.
gap_limitation: Over a decade old; geospatial focus broader than land surveying; does not address racial/gender diversity specifically.

citation: Georgia DOT / ACSM, Meeting the 21st Century Surveying-Geomatics Education Challenge. ROSAP/DOT repository.
key_finding: Lack of traditional student interest + retirement replacement issues + technology change forced Georgia surveying-geomatics community to seek alternative educational approaches.
gap_limitation: State-specific; does not address diversity directly; focused on education pipeline.

citation: Holland S, The Point of Beginning Initiative: Strengthening the Geomatics Workforce. SAGES 2025 conference paper.
key_finding: US facing critical shortage of geomatics professionals; initiative to strengthen workforce pipeline.
gap_limitation: Conference paper; may address diversity but details not available from search snippet alone.

citation: ASCE, Demographic Profile Report. ASCE DEI publications.
data_used: ASEE 2019 data on URM engineering students
key_finding: Provides collective percentages of Underrepresented Minority students in engineering including African American/Black Hispanic Asian American American Indian and Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander.
gap_limitation: Civil engineering focus; useful benchmark for comparison with surveying demographics.

citation: Reskin BF, Occupational Segregation by Gender Race and Ethnicity. Sociological Focus 29(3).
key_finding: Classified 5.8 million workers into 52 race-ethnic-sex groups across 1326 occupation pairs; found sex and race interact in affecting occupational segregation.
gap_limitation: Foundational methodology paper; does not focus on surveying specifically; demonstrates how PUMS microdata can be used for occupation-level diversity analysis.

citation: Equitable Growth, Factsheet: U.S. Occupational Segregation by Race Ethnicity and Gender. Washington Center for Equitable Growth.
key_finding: Duncan Segregation Index shows 56% of Black women (or white men) would need to change occupations for full integration (2016); decline from 59% in 2000.
gap_limitation: Broad labor market analysis; no surveyor-specific findings; useful methodological framework.

citation: The American Surveyor, Bad Backsights: The Topic that Dare Not Speak Its Name. amerisurv.com.
key_finding: Provocative opinion piece addressing workforce issues in surveying including topics the profession avoids discussing openly.
gap_limitation: Trade publication opinion piece; may touch on diversity as taboo topic in profession.

citation: CLGE, Surveying: A Profession Facing a Global Crisis? CLGE white paper.
key_finding: Sub-Saharan Africa: widespread closure of university surveying departments; severe shortage of surveyors for public sector work. Global crisis framing.
gap_limitation: European/international focus; does not address US demographic diversity; old (2008).

citation: BLS, Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics: Surveyors (17-1022). BLS OEWS.
key_finding: Median annual wage for surveyors $73090 (May 2024); detailed employment by state and industry.
gap_limitation: Wage/employment data only; no demographic breakdown in OEWS (demographics come from CPS instead).
